Coram :

Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Saurabh Banerjee
 Order

The petitioner, vide the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973, seek quashing of FIR No.340/2016 dated 17.11.2016 registered under Sections 323/354/506/509/498A/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 at P.S. Subzi Mandi, Delhi and all proceedings emanating therefrom in view of the Compromise Deed dated 18.10.2023 arrived at between the parties.
2.

This petition is accompanied by the Compromise Deed dated 18.10.2023 [Annexure-P-2] and is also supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
3.
Petitioner nos.1 to 9 and as also respondent no.2 are present in CRL.M.C. 9239/2023 page 1 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 18/12/2023 at 22:29:44 Court and have been identified by the IO.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
4. Issue Notice.
5. Learned APP accepts notice.
He confirms that he has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.
6. Learned counsel for the respondent no.2 also accepts notice.
Respondent no.2 confirms that the Harshit Gupta And Ors vs The State Of Delhi Nct And Anr on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155032361/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 29.11.2023.

She further affirms the Compromise Deed dated 18.10.2023 whereby the petitioner no.1 has already paid her a sum of Rs.3,70,00,000/- in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony, maintenance (present, past and future), stridhan etc.
She states that she has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

7. Upon consideration of the existing peculiar facts and the overall events unfolding in their entirety,
even though this Court is mindful that the FIR has been registered under Section 354 IPC, this Court is inclined to quash the present FIR in exercise of its inherent powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C.,
particularly whence it would be in the interest of justice and will also be in the interest of the parties and betterment of their future.

Further, since a settlement has been arrived at between the parties,
and as the respondent no.2 does not wish to continue with the criminal proceedings, to bring a quietus to the present disputes and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 SCC 466 and as also held by a Co-ordinate CRL.M.C. 9239/2023 page 2 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.

sentences.text: 8. Accordingly, the petition is allowed and FIR No.340/2016 dated 07.11.2016 registered under Sections 323/354/506/509/498A/34 IPC at P.S. Subzi Mandi, Delhi and all proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed, subject to the petitioners collectively depositing a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- with the Delhi Police Welfare Society Fund [Account No.18200100001081 and IFSC Code-UCBA0001820] within a period of one week.
Acknowledgement slip in respect of payment of costs be supplied to the Investigating Officer within a period of two days thereafter.

9. Needless to state that the settlement arrived at between the parties resulting in closure of all criminal proceedings inter se the parties by way of the present order will, in no way, effect the rights of the children of the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 namely Master Pragyan vis-a-vis his parents, as may be available under law, in any manner whatsoever.
10. The petition alongwith the pending application stands disposed of.

11. List the matter for compliance on 15.01.2024.
